header: Sound CPU: a sequencer for the 8-voice 15XX WSG (ported as
REQUESTS. The main CPU asks for sound n (0-25) by writing 1 to
snd_request+n ($0040+n here, main $6040+n); the sub CPU cannot reach
this RAM and queues its requests in $0840+n, which the main task
task_sound_queue ($D8B0) forwards once a frame. Sound $16 (coin) is a
count (INC), every other request byte is a flag. Retriggered sounds
(1, 7, $0A-$0E) restart on every new request; the others play while
their request byte is set, and op_end clears it when the stream ends.
The main CPU stops a sound early by clearing snd_request+n and
EACH FRAME (irq_sound): the voice shadow $0080 (vol, freq lo, mid,
hi|wave per voice) goes to the WSG and is cleared; then sounds 0-25 in
order each run one frame (play_sound); a later sound overwrites the
shadow of a voice it shares with an earlier one, so it wins. A sound
owns WSG voices sound_voice[n].., a 17-byte channel block per voice
(sound_channels[n]) and a header (sound_headers[n]) of note streams.
Every voice steps a volume envelope and a note stream (next_note).

E000.name: reset_sound
doc: Power-on of the sound CPU (released by the main CPU's SRESET write):
mask the IRQ latch; spin (kicking the watchdog) until the main CPU
writes $11 to $0040; checksum $E000-$FFFF (non-zero sum -> $0380 =
1); answer $22 in $0040; clear $0000-$02FF (the WSG registers and
the handshake byte too, about 700 cycles after the $22 was written:
the main CPU must have seen it by then); copy the 32 tempo bytes
$E3EF-$E40E to $00A0; S = $0400; enable the IRQ and idle in BRA *
- all further work happens in irq_sound.
QUIRK: the watchdog kick at $E050 uses the odd address $2007 (any
$2000-$3FFF access kicks it); LDY $3000 at $E02D kicks it twice.

E053.name: idle_forever
doc: BRA *: the CPU only runs its IRQ from now on (3 cycles a pass,
which sets the IRQ's entry latency).

E055.name: irq_sound
doc: Sound CPU vblank IRQ.
1. acknowledge (IRQ latch off) and kick the watchdog;
2. copy the voice shadow $0080-$009F into the WSG: per voice v,
shadow bytes vol, freq lo, freq mid, freq hi|wave go to WSG
registers 8v+3..8v+6, then clear the shadow (silence unless a
sound writes it again this frame);
3. for each sound n = 0..25 in order (one unrolled slot each): a
held sound runs play_sound while snd_request+n is set, else its
snd_active+n is cleared so it starts from the top next time; a
retriggered sound (1, 7, $0A-$0E) clears both bytes on a request
(a restart) and runs while snd_active+n is set. Later sounds win
the voices they share;
4. snd_irq_done = 1, re-enable the IRQ latch, RTI.
The port charges the MAME cycle of every instruction and yields
before each access to $0040-$007F, which the main CPU shares.

E233.name: play_sound
doc: Run sound snd_current (n) for one frame. snd_voice = its first WSG
voice (sound_voice[n]); X = its channel blocks (sound_channels[n]),
17 bytes per voice:
+0/1 note stream pointer   +2 frequency table number x 2
+3 waveform (bits 4-6, ORed into freq hi)  +4 envelope number
+5 volume ($F0 = resting)  +6/7/8 frequency hi|wave / mid / lo
+9 frames left in the note  +A envelope position
+B ramp counter ($FF = idle)  +C/+E/+F loop counters (F3/F5/F6)
+D flag set by F4 (F3 loops pass straight through)
+$10 = $11 in the last block of the sound
On the first frame (snd_active+n = 0) set snd_active+n and build the
blocks from the header (sound_headers[n]): per voice a stream
pointer (the stream's first two bytes are the waveform and the
envelope) and a frequency table number, until $11; each voice
fetches its first note (next_note) and its loop counters start at 0.
Then play_voice runs every voice once.
QUIRK: if a stream ended (op_end) during this set-up, op_end's
PULS X,U / RTS would pop the X pushed at $E252 as a return address
and run RAM; no stream in the ROM does that (the port throws).

E27F.name: play_voice
doc: Play every voice of the sound for one frame, from block X and voice
snd_voice on: step the volume envelope (skipped while resting: +5 =
$F0 is written as the volume, whose low nibble 0 is silence), write
volume and frequency to the shadow (write_shadow), count the note
down and fetch the next one. Returns after the block whose +$10 is
$11, or straight to irq_sound when a stream ends (op_end).

E285.name: envelope_step
doc: One step of voice X's volume envelope: the byte at position +A of
envelope +4 (envelopes table) is a level 0-$F (play it, advance)
or an op $10-$16, dispatched on its low nibble through envelope_ops
with U = the op's address. next_note restarts the envelope (+A = 0)
for every note and rest.

E29F.name: envelope_ops
doc: Envelope ops $10 sustain, $12 sustain and fade out, $14 repeat, $16
ramp (the low nibble is the byte offset into this table, so only
even values are valid).

E2A7.name: env_op_ramp
doc: Envelope op $16 n: a linear decay. The first frame (+B = $FF) takes
the previous level - 1 as the counter +B; each frame plays the
counter and lowers it; once it reaches n + 1 it is played again,
+B goes back to $FF and the position moves onto n, which the next
frame plays as an ordinary level (e.g. 7 7 16 00 10: 7 7 6 5 4 3 2
1 1 0 0 ...). Named 'hold' in the port.
QUIRK: with n >= previous level - 1 the counter would pass n + 1,
wrap to $FF (full volume) and restart; no envelope in the ROM does.

E2C8.name: env_op_loop
doc: Envelope op $14: repeat the envelope from its first level.

E2CC.name: env_op_keep
doc: Envelope op $10: sustain - play the level before it for the rest
of the note.

E2D0.name: env_op_limit
doc: Envelope op $12: sustain the level before it, but no louder than the
frames left in the note (+9): the note fades out over its last 15
frames.

E2DC.name: write_shadow
doc: Store voice X's volume (A -> +5) and frequency in the shadow at
$0080 + 4 x snd_voice: vol, freq lo, freq mid, freq hi|wave (the
order of WSG registers 3-6). Entered at $E2DA (env_advance) the
envelope position +A is advanced first. Then count the note down
(+9) and fetch the next event when it runs out; RTS after the last
voice, else on to the next block (+$11) and voice.

E309.name: next_note
doc: Fetch the next event of voice X's note stream (pointer at +0/1):
$00-$BF n, len: a note. High nibble = pitch, the entry of the
voice's frequency table (+2: 0 = A ... 11 = G#), low
nibble = octave shift (the 20-bit frequency is shifted
right that many times, one octave each); the waveform
bits +3 are ORed into the top byte;
$Cx len:  a rest (+5 = $F0);
$F0-$F7:  a command through stream_ops (op_end ends the sound).
The length byte times the sound's tempo (snd_tempo+n, MUL, low byte
only) is the note's duration in frames (+9); the envelope restarts
QUIRK: only the low byte of the MUL is kept (length x tempo above
255 wraps, 0 plays 256 frames); pitch nibbles $D/$E would read past
the 12-entry table. No stream does either.

E369.name: stream_command
doc: Stream byte $F0-$F7: dispatch its low nibble through stream_ops,
with U = the stream pointer and B = the byte after the command.
Every op but op_end continues at set_stream_ptr (next event).
QUIRK: $F8-$FF would jump through the code after the table; no
stream uses them.

E376.name: stream_ops
doc: Note stream commands $F0-$F7.

E386.name: op_jump
doc: $F7 addr: continue the stream at addr.

E38A.name: op_wave
doc: $F1 n: waveform bits (+3); n >> 4 is the WSG waveform 0-7.

E38E.name: op_envelope
doc: $F2 n: volume envelope n (+4), from the next note on.

E392.name: op_set_d
doc: $F4 n: set the flag +D; while it is non-zero every $F3 loop passes
straight through. Unused by the ROM's streams.

E398.name: op_loop_c
doc: $F3 n, addr: repeat - jump to addr until the counter +C, counted up
on every pass, equals n (the section runs n times); passes straight
through while +D is set.
QUIRK: +C is never reset, so a second $F3 in the same voice would
count on from n (256 - n more passes); no stream has two.

E3A4.name: op_loop_f
doc: $F6 n, addr: count +F up; on its n-th pass clear it and jump to
addr, else go on (a jump taken every n-th time).

E3AE.name: op_loop_e
doc: $F5 n, addr: count +E up; jump to addr on the pass where it equals
n (only once: +E is not cleared), else go on.

E3BF.name: op_end
doc: $F0: end of the sound. Clear its request byte (sound $16, the coin
sound, counts coins and is decremented instead, so it plays once
per coin) and its active byte, then return straight to irq_sound:
PULS X,U drops next_note's saved U and its return into write_shadow
(voice_done), and the RTS leaves play_sound. The first voice to
reach $F0 ends the whole sound: the voices after it are not played
this frame, and none of them is played again.

E3D5.name: sound_voice
doc: First WSG voice (0-7) used by each sound 0-25; voice k of the
sound's header plays on WSG voice sound_voice[n] + k.

E3EF.name: tempo_init
doc: Tempo per sound 0-25: the frames per unit of note length (copied
with 6 more bytes to snd_tempo at boot).
QUIRK: the copy is 32 bytes; the last six (tempos of sounds 26-31,
never played) are the first bytes of sound_channels.

E409.name: sound_channels
doc: Channel block address in RAM of each sound 0-25 (17 bytes per
voice, $0100-$0352). Sounds that should never play together share
blocks: the tunes 0, 2-6, 8, $12, $14, $17, $18 all start at $0100;
QUIRK: when two sounds sharing blocks do play at once, the second
one's first frame rebuilds the blocks from its own header, and from
then on both step the same streams each frame until one ends: a coin
($16) 10 frames into the extra-ship jingle ($15) makes the pair last
119 frames instead of 71 and 73, garbled.

E40F.name: tempo_copy_end
doc: End of the 32-byte tempo copy (the CMPX at $E042): the seventh
byte of sound_channels.

E43D.name: sound_headers
doc: Header of each sound 0-25 (hdr_<name> below): per voice a note
stream pointer and a frequency table number, $11 ends the list.

E5D2.name: envelopes
doc: The 31 volume envelopes (env_0 ... env_30 below): levels 0-$F, one
a frame, then an op: $10 sustain the last level, $12 sustain but
fade out with the note's last frames, $14 repeat, $16 n ramp down
one step a frame to n (see env_op_ramp). Each line below shows the
decoded envelope.

E6D2.name: freq_tables
doc: The three frequency tables, 12 notes A..G# of 3 bytes each (freq
bits 16-19, 8-15, 0-7; the tone is freq x 24000 / 2^20 Hz); an
unused $00 follows each. A stream's octave shift divides by 2^n.

E6D8.name: freq_low
doc: Frequency table 0: A7 = 3496 Hz, 12 cents below A440 pitch (the
detuned twin of freq_a440 for chorus voices).

E6FD.name: freq_a440
doc: Frequency table 1: equal temperament at A440 pitch, A7 = 3520 Hz.

E722.name: freq_high
doc: Frequency table 2: A7 = 3544 Hz, 12 cents above A440 pitch.

FFEF.name: checksum_E000
doc: Checksum adjust: the byte sum of $E000-$FFFF is 0 (tested by
reset_sound; an error is reported to the main CPU in $0380).

comments.E268: stream now past those two bytes
comments.E297: envelope op in the low nibble
comments.E2B6: ramp done: idle, move onto n
comments.E2D2: no louder than the frames left
comments.E3B2: jump only on the n-th pass
comments.E3D2: drop next_note's U and the return to play_voice: RTS goes back to irq_sound

E747: NOTE STREAMS ($E747-$FA3D). A stream starts with its waveform byte
(bits 4-6) and its envelope number; then notes $pn,len (pitch p of
the voice's frequency table, n octaves down), rests $Cx,len and
commands $F0-$F7 (stream_ops). Shown as pitch:length, e.g. C6:4 =
C6 for 4 x tempo frames; -:6 = a rest of 6. Labels: <sound>_v<k> =
voice k of that sound's header; lXXXX = a jump or loop target.

data.name: copyright_text
doc: Copyright text, never read.

names.name: start_tune
doc: Game start music: start_game ($CE17), the main CPU waits for the request to clear ($CE7F); also the demo's start. 384 frames.

names.name: shot
doc: Fighter shot, normal fighter picture $2F (task_player_fire $D1B5). 18 frames.

names.name: challenge_tune
doc: Challenging stage tune: task_stage_clear ($D6E3) when the next stage is a challenging stage (dat_D6E8). 144 frames.

names.name: entry_tune_1st
doc: TOP 5 name entry music for a new best score (rank 1, $B52F via entry_music_ptr). 576 frames.

names.name: entry_tune
doc: TOP 5 name entry music for ranks 2-5 ($B542-$B57B). 960 frames.

names.name: stage_tune
doc: Stage start ("PARSEC nn") jingle: after the start tune ($CE92), at a stage clear ($D6BB), after a lost ship or a player change ($DCFF, $DDE8) and after the challenging-stage results ($E3EC). 108 frames.

names.name: payout_tune
doc: Challenging-stage results pay-out: a component moving into place (payout_lucky) or dropping (payout_byebye). 280 frames.

names.name: shot_upgraded
doc: The fighter's shot when its picture ($0EA2) is not $2F, i.e. after an upgrade (task_player_fire $D1BB; the main listing calls it the dual fighter's); never requested together with sound 1. 31 frames.

names.name: button_wait
doc: Results bonus: requested every frame while the screen waits for a fire press (results_show_bonus $E35F), stopped with snd_active by the press. 20 frames a pass.

names.name: formation_hum
doc: The formation's background hum: sub task_formation_anim ($E34B, via the queue) every frame while the formation is assembled and no refill is flying in. 168 frames a pass.

names.name: hit_challenge
doc: Enemy hit in a challenging stage (task_shot_hits $D3F1 with $115F set), sub bonus_fly ($BDC5) and the last hit counted on the results screen ($E2C4). 39 frames.

names.name: hit
doc: Enemy hit in a normal stage (task_shot_hits $D3F8); a captured ship hit by an enemy shot (task_shot_collisions $FA57). 28 frames.

names.name: flyin
doc: An enemy flying into the formation: sub task_formation_refill ($EA75) and task_escort_flyin_a ($EC5A). 87 frames.

names.name: dive
doc: Enemies leaving the formation to attack: sub launch_group1_tail ($FBF0), launch_group2_tail ($FCE6), task_launch_trio ($FDC5) and formation_home ($B28A). 104 frames.

names.name: special_object
doc: The object at formation_flags+42 starts (sub task_start_188A_object $FE71). 89 frames.

names.name: object_spawn
doc: An object placed at a pseudo-random position (sub object_spawn_random $B967). 120 frames.

names.name: capture
doc: Sub task_capture_steer ($E6C3) every frame while it moves the fighter and the beam sprite (capture_state 1), and bonus_seq_fall ($F6DB). 120 frames a pass.

names.name: effect_rise
doc: Power-up effect 0, six rising sprites (sub effect_rising $B5BA); irq_main clears it at $C07A when a coin ends the demo. 120 frames a pass.

names.name: effect_spread
doc: Power-up effect 1, six sprites spread along the ship (sub effect_sequence $B3F4). 120 frames.

names.name: powerup
doc: Fighter upgrade and power-up effects 2-5 (sub effect_setup $B87B). 72 frames.

names.name: player_explode
doc: The fighter explodes (player_dies $DA0B; the main CPU waits for it at $DA16); task_sound_queue keeps it while player_dying. 540 frames.

names.name: extra_ship
doc: Extra fighter: bonus life (bonus_first/second/every_p1/p2), results pay-out (payout_extend), the bonus ship caught (task_bonus_ship $FE99), sub bonus_seq_extend ($F789). 72 frames.

names.name: coin
doc: Coin: irq_main INCs it per credit ($C05C); op_end counts it down, so it plays once per coin. 74 frames.

names.name: count_tick
doc: Challenging-stage results: one hit counted, every other frame (results_count_hits $E2B2). 4 frames.

names.name: star_warp
doc: Starfield event: stage_event1_step0 ($EAD7, every frame for 60 frames in mode 1) and stage_event5_step0 ($EBA0). 960 frames.

names.name: bonus_ship
doc: The bonus ship appears (task_bonus_ship $FE6A). 35 frames.

0040.name: snd_request
0040.comment: sound n requested: main writes 1 ($16 coin: a count), op_end clears; +0 is also the boot handshake ($11 / $22)

0060.name: snd_active
0060.comment: sound n started: play_sound sets it on the first frame; cleared by op_end, by the IRQ when a held sound is no longer requested and on a retrigger

0080.name: wsg_shadow
0080.comment: voice shadow, 4 bytes per voice: vol, freq lo, mid, hi|wave; to WSG regs 8v+3..8v+6 and cleared every IRQ

00A0.name: snd_tempo
00A0.comment: frames per note length unit of each sound (tempo_init)

00C2.name: snd_irq_done
00C2.comment: set to 1 at the end of every IRQ; nothing reads it

00C3.name: snd_temp
00C3.comment: scratch: pitch x 2 (next_note), ramp end n + 1 (env_op_ramp)

0100.name: snd_blocks
0100.comment: channel blocks, 17 bytes per voice (sound_channels, play_sound), $0100-$0352
